items.event_time_ist: 8 a.m. MDT advisory, Oct 12 (1400 GMT); CNN update ~12:30 PM PDT, Oct 12
items.summary: Hurricane Simon continued weakening Monday: CNN (~12:30 PM PDT) reports 105 mph per the latest NHC update; the 8 a.m. MDT NHC advisory had 110 mph with the center ~55 mi west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, moving northwest at just 3 mph. CNN reports landfall now expected sometime Thursday with winds near 100 mph; an AccuWeather expert says Simon could ultimately stall and never make a true landfall as an organized storm. The hurricane warning (Playa Perula to El Roblito plus Las Islas Marias) remains in effect.
items.title: Hurricane Simon downgraded to Category 2 as it crawls off Mexico's Pacific coast

items.event_time_ist: Announced at a news conference, Oct 12
items.summary: First reported Mexico casualty from Simon: an elderly person died in the southwestern state of Guerrero, according to Mexico's national Civil Protection coordinator during a news conference with President Claudia Sheinbaum. Sheinbaum described overall damage from Simon as 'minor,' saying Guerrero saw the most damage though less than expected, with some damage in Colima; she noted that Tropical Storm Rachel's impacts in Baja California were greater.
items.title: First reported Mexico death from Simon: elderly person in Guerrero

items.event_time_ist: Closures in effect since 6 p.m. local time, Oct 10
items.summary: Both of Mexico's main Pacific tourist airports are shut: Puerto Vallarta International will stay closed until 8 a.m. local time Tuesday, Oct 13 (extended, per Pacific Airport Group), and Manzanillo's airport has suspended all commercial flights — airlines canceled every scheduled flight over the storm threat, per GAP aviation notices. Both airports stopped operating at 6 p.m. local time Oct 10. Mexico's navy has also closed navigation at ports including Puerto Vallarta and Manzanillo.
items.title: Manzanillo airport flights suspended; Puerto Vallarta closure extended to Tuesday morning

items.summary: Simon's slow crawl brought flooding to Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port: heavy rain flooded homes and streets overnight into Sunday, with soldiers and the National Guard deployed to assist families — residents in the Alameda neighborhood waded through shin-deep water while troops bucketed water from homes. Mexico's civil protection agency kept 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima at its highest cyclone alert level and another 93 at high alert.
items.title: Heavy rain floods homes and streets in Manzanillo; soldiers assist residents

items.summary: Simon's remnant moisture is headed for the U.S.: the Weather Prediction Center has outlined an excessive-rainfall risk across parts of the Southern High Plains and Southwest Texas on Wednesday, Oct 14, with 1-2 inches of rain and isolated totals over 3 inches; NWS offices in Lubbock and Amarillo note heavy-rain potential even after the system dissipates. A slight risk of excessive rainfall extends from New Mexico and Texas to Missouri, and a cold front interacting with the remnants brings a Level 2-out-of-5 severe weather threat (hail, tornadoes) to the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles on Tuesday.
items.title: Simon's remnant moisture to fuel heavy rain and flooding across Texas and the Plains midweek

items.source_name: Newsmax / Pensacola News Journal / USA Today
items.summary: Recovery is advancing in Isaias's landfall zone: Destin Mayor Bobby Wagner told Newsmax Monday that ~80% of power is restored in Destin with 100% of water service back, and streets should be cleared of debris today. Florida Power & Light says most affected customers should have power by end of day Monday, Oct 12, with the hardest-hit parts of Escambia and Santa Rosa counties back online Tuesday, Oct 13. In Alabama, ~20,000 homes and businesses remain without power, but Alabama Power says 95% of affected customers are restored.
items.title: Isaias recovery: Destin at ~80% power and 100% water; most FL customers back by Monday night
